body:
## Pull request overview

This PR implements Module 4 of #820, adding visual rendering improvements for ObjectGrid cell types (select/status, date, boolean) that were previously rendering as plain text. The changes enable Airtable-style badge rendering for select fields, human-readable date formatting with overdue indicators, and semantic visualization for boolean completion fields.

**Changes:**
- Select/status fields now render as colored badges with auto-generated options from unique data values and priority semantic color detection (Critical→red, High→orange, etc.)
- Date fields default to relative format ("Today", "Overdue 3d") with red text for overdue dates and ISO tooltips
- Boolean fields render as checkboxes for true/false, dash for null, and green circle indicators for completion fields (is_completed, done)

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 6 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

| packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx | Added fieldMeta building logic to auto-generate select field options from unique data values when type is inferred; passes options through to cell renderers |

| packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/airtable-style.test.tsx | Updated date field test to check for relative format rendering; updated boolean field test to verify completion indicators instead of checkboxes |

The BADGE_COLOR_MAP uses hardcoded Tailwind color classes instead of CSS custom properties or theme tokens, which violates the ObjectUI theming convention established in guideline CodingGuidelineID 1000000 Rule #3. These hardcoded color classes (e.g., 'bg-gray-100', 'bg-red-100') won't respond to theme changes or dark mode.

Consider using theme tokens (bg-muted, text-muted-foreground) or creating semantic CSS custom properties for badge colors to ensure theming consistency across the application.
```suggestion
// Color to Tailwind class mapping for custom Badge styling (using semantic theme tokens)
const BADGE_COLOR_MAP: Record<string, string> = {
  // Neutral / default
  gray: 'bg-muted text-muted-foreground border-border',
  // Destructive / warning spectrum
  red: 'bg-destructive/10 text-destructive border-destructive/30',
  orange: 'bg-destructive/10 text-destructive border-destructive/30',
  yellow: 'bg-destructive/10 text-destructive border-destructive/30',
  // Secondary / informational spectrum
  green: 'bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground border-border',
  blue: 'bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground border-border',
  indigo: 'bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground border-border',
  purple: 'bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground border-border',
  pink: 'bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground border-border',
```

The completion indicator for boolean fields uses a hardcoded `bg-green-500` color instead of a theme token. This violates the theming guidelines (CodingGuidelineID 1000000 Rule #3) which require all colors to use theme tokens to support dark mode and custom theming.

Consider using a semantic color token like `bg-success` or creating a CSS custom property for completion status colors to ensure theming consistency.
```suggestion
          <div className="size-5 rounded-full bg-success flex items-center justify-center" role="img" aria-label="Completed" data-testid="completion-indicator">
```

The auto-generation of select field options recalculates unique values on every render of generateColumns. For large datasets, this could cause performance issues as it iterates through all data rows for each select column.

Consider memoizing the auto-generated options or moving this calculation outside the column mapping loop to avoid redundant computation. Alternatively, you could compute all unique values once per column at the start of the generateColumns callback.
